thread:
zoe: deploy-bot says canary p95 +22% on /embeddings for the v2.6 rollout in US-W. Its proposing an auto-revert. Can someone with approval weigh in?
deploy-bot: ALERT: Canary p95 +22% vs baseline. Auto-revert threshold reached. Suggested action: auto-rollback. [telemetry link]
oncall: Oncall here. Are we seeing 5xxs or customer errors?
zoe: No 5xxs, only latency increase and a small bump in kvcache misses after a kernel flag change.
kai: We can do a manual partial routing pin for embeddings to v1.5.2 for 50% traffic as a safety-latch. Prefer that over full revert if it reduces p95 quickly.
release-bot: NOTE: Partial routing pin during change window requires release owner + oncall approval. Please confirm.
zoe: I approve the partial pin. Kai, please run the pin and monitor p95 for 10 minutes.
kai: Executing: ```rwctl route pin --service=embeddings --version=1.5.2 --scope=50% --ramp=1m --reason="canary p95 spike"```
kai: Pin in place, ramp to 50% in 60s. Monitoring shows p95 drop ~18% on pinned slice within 90s.
oncall: Good. Ramp to 100% and hold for 10m. If stable, suppress auto-revert.
kai: Completed ramp to 100%. Overall p95 back near baseline, kvcache misses normalized.
deploy-bot: INFO: Auto-revert suppressed due to manual intervention. Telemetry OK.
zoe: Drafting brief: "We observed increased latency for embeddings during a staged rollout. We pinned embeddings routing to the previous stable binary (v1.5.2) and paused further rollout. No user-facing errors observed. Engineering investigating kernel flag interaction." Posting to #release-notes and notifying CS.
release-bot: LOG: action recorded. Partial rollback executed by kai; approved by zoe and oncall.
